headline: High: shared file/clipboard and MCP-adjacent workflows create default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk between ChatGPT Desktop and OpenBBTerminal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, and clipboard content, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and a connect-once workflow. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop ingests OpenBBTerminal output via clipboard or files
IF OpenBBTerminal content is routed through an MCP or REST bridge without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools
Use a read-only export format for any handoff
Add a provenance prefix to all OpenBBTerminal outputs
Keep the agents in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data through APIs and Python environments. If the same workspace or copied artifacts are shared, sensitive material can flow from A into B outputs or vice versa. The profiles do not show hard isolation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF the same files or screenshots are shared between the two agents
IF OpenBBTerminal API responses include licensed or financial data that ChatGPT Desktop summarizes or republishes
mitigations: Use separate folders for each agent
Avoid pasting raw outputs between agents
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
Turn off unnecessary file uploads in ChatGPT Desktop
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and OpenBBTerminal also lacks filesystem write and git modification. Their write overlap is therefore limited, so direct destructive conflict is unlikely. The remaining overlap is mainly read/API interaction, which fits low severity.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access not shown in the profiles
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced outside the documented capabilities
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Use manual handoff instead of shared state
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate summaries from files and app context, and OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP/REST inputs. If OpenBBTerminal treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into financial analysis or downstream actions. Because no verification step is documented, the interaction is risky in default workflows.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes ChatGPT-generated text without independent verification
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to summarize market data that OpenBBTerminal then operationalizes
mitigations: Require source links for every claim
Cross-check outputs against primary data
Mark ChatGPT output as untrusted draft text
Use a second reviewer for any action-taking step
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can process uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. If regulated financial or personal data is moved between them, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated financial data or personal data is transferred from OpenBBTerminal into ChatGPT Desktop
IF retention or deletion requirements differ for the same dataset across the two tools
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Strip identifiers before transfer
Confirm retention settings for both tools
Keep audit logs of transfers
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
